dispositions.disposition: Linux subreaper adopts orphaned forks. A 50 ms supervisor guard compares the frozen 180 CPU-second limit against supervisor-reaped CPU plus active/zombie process-group self/reaped child ticks. It rereads parents before children to avoid double counting a child reaped during scanning; monotone sampled maximum handles temporary undercount. Per-process hard CPU/AS and 240-second wall guards remain. Final supervisor reaps adopted descendants and charges max(observed final reaped total, sampled peak), identically to each family without summing family copies.

Worker result requires exact summary schema, integer counts, correct artifact kinds/paths, verified content-addressed verification bytes and original snapshot agreement before acceptance. Malformed or partial output remains in completion raw bytes with result null and terminal interrupted status. Recovery retains a valid result diagnostically when the original exit/resource outcome is unknown. Legacy malformed completions are sanitized before any family terminalization; partially terminalized outcomes never rewritten. Valid result artifact-copy errors persist a completed/retryable lifecycle with exact recovery command; no worker rerun.

Worker acknowledgement before candidate import and parent lifecycle record PID, actual PGID, Linux boot ID and /proc start ticks. Launch lower bound closes acknowledgement gaps. Recovery matches exact inherited worker argv, verifies the retained start identity/boot/PGID and rechecks the live process before killpg(actual PGID); surviving fork child PID is never mistaken for PGID. Reused leader PID is excluded, executable survivors retain the gate, and bounded drain waits allow termination to settle.

New lifecycle/configuration explicitly records supervisor path alongside retained supervisor bytes. Recovery validates matching path, exact owning family membership and retained source bytes. Legacy F05-F08 ownership is resolved from acknowledgement or exact family set; foreign unresolved lifecycle reports a shell-quoted command for tools/verify_foundation_extensions.py --recover ID. Recovery never launches a worker or modifies older scripts.

Preflight and recorder pin immutable pre-repair-review SHA368c6373fd4de1a9d92bce73488667815f47d998a3ed0187ebf73bd7ad4b4f12, require exactly seven original reviewer inputs and all original frozen contracts, validate their retained exact bytes/selectors/IDs, recompute the complete 92-finding union and demand exact final disposition keys. Each finding selects one repair_report in retained reports; its exact carried entry must be repaired_and_statically_verified. Unused/missing repair supports rejected; reports may explicitly defer unselected findings to another owner.

Normalizer validates exact protocol/golden artifacts and source preparation bytes against registered source artifact references before deriving mapping. Mappings include protocol among all six exact input identities plus normalizer identity and frozen source/preparation refs. Preflight validates the exact ordered current input list and frozen reference bindings, retains all input bytes and normalizer source. Recorder rechecks source, exact mapping inputs and immutable refs before evidence attachment.

limitations: Static verification only; root owns the one supervised registered run.
CPU is sampled at 50 ms and can exceed the soft threshold by scheduling/poll granularity; observed usage is charged, never clipped. Per-process hard limit remains 190 seconds.
Linux /proc, flock, prctl subreaper and process-group semantics are explicit platform requirements. A supervisor hard crash with unknown usage still charges each family reservation.
RSS is reaped process peak from RUSAGE_CHILDREN, not a sum or isolated component allocation.
Unverifiable legacy current-tool start identity retains reconciliation gate; foreign legacy runs route to their owning unchanged tool.
External effects, market data and economic runs remain outside this work.
